item.title: An Asymptotic for Non-Wieferich Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.28685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A cyclic number is a positive integer $n$ such that $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$. Erd\H{o}s showed that the number of cyclic numbers up to $x$, $C(x)$, has $C(x) \sim e^{-\gamma}x/\log_3(x)$ asymptotically as $x$ tends to infinity. We define Wieferich numbers to be odd, positive integers $n$ such that $(n, (2^{\ell(n)}-1)/n) > 1$, where $\ell(n)$ is the smallest positive integer with $2^{\ell(n)} \equiv 1 \mod n$. Franco and Pomerance showed that non-Wieferich numbers have density zero among the odd integers. We show that the counting function of $n \leq x$ in the symmetric difference of non-Wieferich numbers and cyclic numbers is $O(x/(\log_3(x))^2)$, under a mild assumption on the counting function of Wieferich primes.
item.dc:creator: Casia Siegel

item.title: A Counterexample to the Eventual Stability Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.28688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a counterexample to the eventual stability conjecture over number fields and classify for power maps.
item.dc:creator: Thomas J. Tucker, Zheng Zhu

item.title: Sch\"affer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$
item.description: arXiv:2610.28768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1956, Sch\"affer made a conjecture on the whole number solutions to the Diophantine equation $S_k(x):=1^k+2^k+\cdots+x^k=y^n$. In this paper we show how for even $k$, we can descend to a long list of three coupled equations of the form $Ax^p-By^p=1$, where $A,B\in\mathbb{Q}$. To this system, we apply the modular method, linear forms in logarithms, and local methods. As a result, we prove Sch\"affer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$.
item.dc:creator: Imin Chen, Stephen Choi, James Houle

item.title: A quaternary Diophantine inequality with prime numbers of a special form (II)
item.dc:creator: Yuhua Zhao, Jinjiang Li, Linji Long, Min Zhang

item.title: A relative Schinzel-Zassenhaus bound for the polynomial $T^2 - 1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.28782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $f(T) = T^2 - 1$, we establish a lower bound for the relative dynamical house of wandering algebraic integers. This bound depends on the degree over the maximal abelian extension of the rationals. Our proof follows Dimitrov's approach to the Schinzel-Zassenhaus Conjecture and its generalization by Habegger-Schmidt.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Cangini

item.title: Short sums of the M\"obius function over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.28822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new method which allows us to estimate, with a power saving, sums of the M{\"o}bius function over function fields $\F_p(X)$. The sums run over monic polynomials with all other coefficients in short intervals, of length below the P\'olya--Vinogradov threshold $p^{1/2}$. A classical result of L.~Stickelberger (1898) reduces this question to bounding character sums with polynomial discriminants which are inhomogeneous multivariate polynomials. Variants of Burgess's method with non-linear shifts {\it {\`a} la carte} are introduced to go beyond the P\'olya--Vinogradov range, combined with a stratification result of J. Xu (2020) for complete character sums.
item.dc:creator: Etienne Fouvry, Igor E. Shparlinski, Ping Xi

item.title: Subset sums of power values over Galois rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.28837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R=GR(p^m,p^{mf})$, where $p$ is prime, $q=p^f$, $m,f\geq1$, $d\geq2$ and $p\nmid d$. We count $n$-element subsets of $P=\{x^d:x\in R\}\setminus\{0\}$, the set of distinct nonzero $d$th-power values, with a prescribed sum. For fixed $m,d,n$ with $n\geq3$, the count equals \[ q^{-m}\binom{|P|}{n}(1+O_{m,d,n}(q^{1-n/2})) \] as $q\to\infty$ through admissible prime powers, uniformly over all targets and with both $p$ and $f$ allowed to vary. For fixed $m,d$, we also classify uniform relative equidistribution at the remaining positive sizes: it fails at $n=1$, and at $n=2$ it holds along an admissible sequence if and only if, for all sufficiently large terms, $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$ and $(m\geq2\text{ or }p\ne2)$.
item.dc:creator: Zijie Gu

item.title: On a conjecture of Velani
item.description: arXiv:2610.28839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hat{\mu}(2^k)|^\sigma < \infty$ for any $\sigma > 0$, where $\mu$ is the Cantor measure.
item.dc:creator: Sam Chow, Han Yu

item.title: Hecke Orbits on Globally Drinfeld-Uniformized Shimura Varieties Are $p$-adically Nowhere Dense
item.description: arXiv:2610.28869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fix a projective unitary Shimura datum satisfying Varshavsky's global Drinfeld uniformization hypotheses at a place $v\mid p$ of its reflex field $E$. Let $\mathcal{S}h$ be the base change of the Shimura variety to $\mathbb C_p$ at a sufficiently small neat finite level. We prove that for every closed reduced algebraic subvariety $Z\subset\mathcal{S}h$ with $\operatorname{dim} Z<\operatorname{dim} \mathcal{S}h$, the $p$-adic closure of its full finite adelic Hecke orbit has empty interior in $\mathcal{S}h(\mathbb C_p)$. At certain compatible levels, the nowhere density theorem also holds for Shimura varieties associated with a related PEL datum having the same adjoint datum as Varshavsky's. Moreover, for every rational prime $p$ and every integer $d\geq2$, there is a projective unitary Shimura variety of dimension $d-1$ satisfying these uniformization hypotheses at a place above $p$ for which the nowhere density theorem holds.
item.dc:creator: Yu Fu

item.title: The Octonionic Rational Wave Numbers: Non-Associative Sequence Algebras, Moufang Loops, and Exceptional $G_2$ Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize discrete rational wave numbers (arXiv:2609.23233) to the octonionic rational wave numbers $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ over Cayley's octonions $\mathbb{O}$. Rather than assuming higher imaginary units, all rational wave number spaces $\mathbb{C}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ are derived constructively from two scalar primitives: the coordinate advance $E_Z$ and phase calibration $E_{\bar{1}}$. Their closure under pointwise multiplication, inversion, and rational roots generates an infinite divisible Moufang loop on the sequence ring $\mathcal{S}_\mathbb{O} := \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$, terminating strictly at $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ via sedenionic zero-divisor excision. By Artin's Theorem, pairwise compositions remain strictly associative, whereas three-wave interactions generate an intrinsic non-associative curvature quantified by the associator $[u, v, w] = (uv)w - u(vw)$. We define a real-valued sequence inner product that bypasses the Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner obstruction, establishing the orthonormality of the seven Fano coordinate primitives. We establish three principal theorems: (1) The Invariant Hexagonal Mesh Theorem, proving that cumulative integration exhibits a scale-invariant bifurcation at $n=6$ governed by the root system of $G_2 = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$ and its $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ stabilizer subgroup; (2) The Algebraic Phase Jitter Theorem, showing that Catalan parenthesization trees across non-Fano triads produce an irreducible zero-point phase fluctuation, yielding an algebraic origin for vacuum jitter; and (3) The Rational Loop Closure Theorem, proving that rational frequencies select closed finite Moufang sub-loops, while irrational frequencies yield topologically dense, non-closing trajectories. This provides an autonomous, discrete algebraic foundation for non-associative geometry and fundamental physical symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Terence R. Smith

item.title: Zeros of quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Dirichlet $L$-functions $L(s, \chi)$ where $\chi$ is a quadratic character to modulus $q$. We show that for $\chi$ even (resp. odd) $L(\sigma, \chi)\neq 0$ for all $\sigma >0$ provided that $q\leq 10^{9}$ (resp. $q\leq 10^{10})$. In particular, this result rules out Siegel--Landau zeros for such $L$-functions. Combined, these results improve on previous work by nearly four orders of magnitude. We also list some applications of this work.
item.dc:creator: Dave Platt, Tim Trudgian

item.title: Construction of Galois modules describing ideal class groups and applications to Iwasawa theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.29071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, the ideal class groups of intermediate fields do not behave well under taking Galois coinvariants in general. In this paper, we construct a Galois module whose Galois coinvariants explicitly describe the ideal class groups of the intermediate fields. As an application, we demonstrate how this construction naturally yields some results in classical Iwasawa theory.
item.dc:creator: Takenori Kataoka

item.title: Mixed sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values with restricted indices
item.description: arXiv:2610.29100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study arithmetic sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values subject to upper or lower bounds on their indices. Let $\eta(\mathcal D_q)$ be the image, under the zeta-star correspondence, of the admissible infinite index sequences with all indices at most $q$, and let $\overline{\eta(\mathcal T_p)}$ be the closure of the image of the sequences with all indices at least $p$. We prove that $\eta(\mathcal D_q)+\overline{\eta(\mathcal T_p)}$ is an interval exactly when $p\leq q$; in that case it is $[\zeta^\star(\{q\}^{\infty})+1,\infty)$. We also show that sums of two upper-bounded sets are half-lines, even with different bounds, whereas sums of two lower-bounded sets are never intervals. The proofs combine a uniform product estimate with natural gap constructions. Lateral thickness handles the diagonal case $p=q\geq3$, while a non-strict local bridge--gap criterion treats $p=q=2$ directly. Compact truncations and explicit omitted intervals yield the remaining assertions.
item.dc:creator: Jiangtao Li, Siyu Yang

item.title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
item.description: arXiv:2610.29305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: Ofir Gorodetsky

item.title: Ideal class groups of certain real quadratic number fields and factorizations of values of certain quadratic polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $d-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive odd integers $x\leq\sqrt{p}$. We also determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $2p-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive even integers $x\leq\sqrt{2p}$. To this end, we show that these properties of $p$ and $2p$ impose restrictions on the class numbers and fundamental units of the real quadratic fields ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{p})$ and ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{2p})$.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane R. Louboutin

item.title: Computing Theta Characteristics and their Galois action on general curves of moderate genus
item.description: arXiv:2610.29449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we present an algorithm that, given a smooth curve $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, returns an explicit arithmetic representation of both odd and even Theta Characteristics split by parity. It allows us to retrieve their Galois action and \'etale algebra. The output includes the Theta Hyperplanes of the Theta Characteristics when they are finite, their associated proof functions as well as the dictionary of their quadratic forms. The algorithm works in a rather large generality as it handles any one-equation (potentially singular) model of smooth curves. The most binding requirement remains the necessity for an explicit degree 1 rational divisor on the curve or more likely a rational point. We implemented the algorithm and give examples up to genus $5$.
item.dc:creator: Thibaut Misme

item.title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers within the set of squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.29470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the set of numbers of type $n = 2m^2$ below $X$ which cannot be written as a sum of two primes has cardinality at most $X^{19/24 + o(1)}$.
item.dc:creator: A. Perelli, J. Pintz

item.title: Residue Sums Modulo Products of Two Distinct Odd Primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S_m(a)$ denote the sum of the least positive residues in one multiplicative period of $a$ modulo $m$, of length $k$. We study the equality $S_m(a)=mk/2$ for $m=pq$, where $p,q$ are distinct odd primes and $k$ is even. Complementary pairing settles subgroups containing $-1$; the remaining cases depend on their embedding in the two local unit groups. At index four, we exclude mixed cyclic subgroups with biquadratic annihilator and classify every eligible imprimitive quartic kernel using two odd integer moments at its prime conductor. For each fixed conductor, the proportion of admissible second primes giving equality is $1/4$ or $1/2$; full coset balance has proportion $1/4$. For primitive quartic characters, classical triangular character-sum identities yield explicit short-sum criteria, and the relative class-number formula gives an obstruction to a centered coset. At index six, we give structural counts and construct an infinite family modulo $19q$ in which nonzero sextic and quadratic moments cancel. These applications use a standard odd-character expansion, which also recovers the known index-two balance classification and determines the sign of its deviation. A reproducible census for $pq\le10000$ counts $75\,090$ eligible cyclic subgroups and identifies $101$ mixed index-four subgroups whose own sum is centered although some coset sums are not.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Mircea Merca, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Perturbing the Conway sequence
item.description: arXiv:2610.29631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the alternating perturbation of Conway's nested recurrence, $C(n)=C(C(n-1))+C(n-C(n-1))+(-1)^n$ for $n\geq 3$, with $C(1)=C(2)=1$. We prove that the sequence is well defined and satisfies $C(n)=\psi^{-3}n+O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, where $\psi>1$ is the real root of $\psi^3=\psi^2+1$.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Cloitre

item.title: On the Gauss sphere problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.29636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we improve Heath-Brown's estimate for the error term in the three-dimensional sphere problem, proving \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}=\frac{4\pi}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{55/42+\varepsilon}). \] Incoporating the recent OpenAI quasi-GRH into our argument further improves this to \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}= \frac{4\pi}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{\frac{2274811}{1743872}+\varepsilon}). \]
item.dc:creator: Chiara Bellotti, Bryce Kerr

item.title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{\xi\in \mathbb F_q^d:\xi_1^2+\cdots+\xi_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, d\sigma)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $\eta_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $\eta_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Boqing Xue

item.title: Integer symplectic matrices in expanding boxes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an essentially optimal uniform upper bound for the number of integer symplectic matrices inside a box of expanding side length and arbitrary centre.
item.dc:creator: Lena Wurzinger

item.title: Integral trace forms of cyclic number fields without tameness
item.description: arXiv:2610.29876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K/\mathbf{Q}$ be a cyclic number field and let $T_K=\bigl(\mathcal{O}_K,(x,y)\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbf{Q}}(xy)\bigr)$ be its integral trace lattice. We prove that two cyclic number fields have isometric integral trace lattices if and only if they have the same degree, signature, and signed discriminant. More generally, an isomorphism between the Dirichlet character groups of two finite abelian extensions that preserves the conductor and parity of every character yields an isometry of their integral trace lattices, equivariant for the dual identification of Galois groups. For cyclic fields, the degree, signature, and discriminant determine the character group together with these two functions. This proves Bola\~nos's conjecture for wildly ramified cyclic fields and gives the corresponding extension of the tame classification: in general, the signature must be retained as an additional invariant.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Lin Zhang

item.title: On the notion of reasonable functions in Cohen--Lenstra type heuristics
item.description: arXiv:2610.29880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We elucidate the notion of "reasonable functions" in the context of Cohen--Lenstra heuristics. For a sequence $(x_i)_i$ of independent random variables valued in an infinite discrete probability space $(X,p)$, we investigate for what sets $S$ of functions on $X$ it is true that almost surely, for all $f\in S$, the average of $f$ on the sequence is equal to its expected value. We show that if $p$ decays sufficiently quickly, as e.g. the Cohen--Lenstra distribution does, then $\bigcup_{q>1}L^q(X)$ is such a set; while if $p$ decays sufficiently slowly, then not even $\bigcap_{q<\infty}L^q(X)$ has this property.
item.dc:creator: Alex Bartel, Adam Morgan

item.title: Squarefree values of random polynomials are Gaussian mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2610.29911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fix $d\ge1$ and choose a polynomial $P$ uniformly at random from the set of integer polynomials of degree $d$ whose coefficients have absolute value at most $H$. We study $E_{P}$, the error in the count of squarefree values $P(n)$ for $n\leq x$. In the range $x=H^{o\left(1\right)}$, we prove that $E_{P}\left(x\right)/x^{\frac{1}{4}}$ converges to a Gaussian mixture that is not itself Gaussian, $\sqrt{C\left(G\right)}Z$, where $G$ is the weak limit, as $H\rightarrow\infty$, of the prime-indexed vector $\left(P\bmod p^{2}\right)_{p}$, $C$ is a nonnegative function and $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian. This answers a question of Sofos. Finally, in the appendix, we establish that $\log \mathbb{E}[C(G)^m]\asymp_d m^2/(\log m)^2$ as $m\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Omer Simhi

item.title: A Sharp Bound for Additive Complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.29963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be infinite sets of nonnegative integers whose sum contains all sufficiently large integers, and let $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ be their counting functions. We give a discrete proof of the sharp implication \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac32 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A(x)B(x)-x\longrightarrow+\infty. \] The constant $3/2$ is best possible. Using finite convolution sums, we show that a long gap in one set forces a gap in the other. We then compare the counting functions before and after the gap to obtain the sharp bound.
item.dc:creator: Zihan Zhang

item.title: Zeros of $E_2$, quasi-periods, and Schwarz maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.30025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the zeros of the Eisenstein series $E_2$, their distribution near rational cusps, and the values of modular functions at these zeros. Using Watson's inversion formula, we prove that the number of zeros in $0\leq\operatorname{Re}\tau<1$ with imaginary part at least $Y$ satisfies \[ N(Y)=\frac{1}{2\pi Y} +O\!\left(Y^{-1/2}\log\frac1Y\right) \qquad(Y\to0^+). \] We also determine the limiting distribution of the scaled displacements from the cusps and prove that two zeros whose difference is rational differ by an integer. At every zero $\rho$, classical transcendence theorems imply that both $j(\rho)$ and $\lambda(\rho)$ are transcendental. We use this fact to obtain an exact multiplicity formula for arithmetic quasimodular forms at arbitrary congruence level and to show that all ordinary derivatives of arithmetic modular functions on congruence subgroups, evaluated at $\rho$, are algebraic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}(j(\rho),j'(\rho))$. We then relate Watson's formula to the Schwarz map of a rational transform of the Legendre hypergeometric equation. Finally, we give conditional results on the transcendence of $\rho$ under modular Schanuel and period conjectures, and determine why the associated analytic subgroup fails the rank condition in Waldschmidt's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Abdellah Sebbar

item.title: Support periods of polynomials and support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes over Galois rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.29284v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let \(A=\GR(p^e,r)\) have residue field \(\F_q\), and let \(\lambda\in A^\times\). We relate coefficient compression of monic divisors of \(X^N-\lambda\) to support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes. At a simple-root length, the support period of every nonconstant monic divisor is preserved at each coefficient precision and equals the order of the multiplicative stabilizer of its root set. For a cyclic Frobenius-orbit polynomial, the multiple equal-difference structure determines its support period, core degree, and least relative degree of an unramified extension over which all its basic-irreducible factors are binomials. Coordinate projections give every constacyclic code over a finite commutative ring a unique maximal interleaving into copies of one support-primitive code. At simple-root lengths over \(A\), the intrinsic period of a code is the greatest common divisor of the periods of its torsion codes. The decomposition yields distance and duality formulas and the arithmetic Singleton bound for free codes. At every length, a nonzero code over \(A\) has the same minimum Hamming distance as its highest torsion code, which gives a refined bound. At repeated-root lengths, identical torsion filtrations can occur with different intrinsic periods, while a class of nonzero codes obtained by substitution from simple-root generators retains the same core and minimum distance. Trace matrices recover the coefficients of basic-irreducible cores using unit pivots, and local Hensel corrections lift compressed factors directly. For \(X^n-1\) with \(p\nmid n\), lifting and output have quasi-linear bit cost in the compressed representation when the arithmetic data and residue factorizations are given.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhu, Hongfeng Wu

item.title: Local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for unitary groups: Trace formula approach for epsilon dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.29483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a proof independent of the theta-lifting for the epsilon-dichotomy of the local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture of real unitary groups for tempered L-parameters. The approach is based on the local trace formula and endoscopic character identities following Waldspurger and Chen-Luo.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Chen, Xiaowei Li, Bushi Ren

item.title: Homological branching laws for $p$-adic and mod $p$ representations of ${\rm GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field
item.description: arXiv:2610.29629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $p\geq 5$. In this paper, we establish homological branching laws for mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ restricted to split and nonsplit maximal tori, treating principal and special series and, when $F=\mathbb Q_p$, supersingular representations. We determine the derived Hom-complexes in both orders for nonexceptional characters. At exceptional characters, we calculate their Euler--Poincar\'e characteristics under a $p$-torsion-freeness hypothesis. We also establish corresponding results for a class of unitary Banach space representations.
item.dc:creator: Yang Chen, Haoran Wang

item.title: Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.29721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.
item.dc:creator: Phillip Harris, Jiaqi Hou, Xiaoqi Huang

item.title: On Almost MDS codes holding $(n-k-1)$-designs and an open problem on Witt design
item.description: arXiv:2610.29744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an almost maximum distance separable (AMDS) code over the finite fields with parameters $[n,k,n-k]$ whose minimum-weight codewords support an $(n-k-1)$-$(n,n-k,\lambda)$ design. We first determine the parameters of the dual code $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. We also characterize the design and its complementary design supported by the minimum weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. In particular, we present explicit formulas for the weight enumerators of all subset codes of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$ with length at least $k+1$. These formulas are completely determined by the cardinality of the subset, the dimension, together with the parameter $\lambda$, and are independent of the specific choice of subsets. As an application, we answer an open problem posed by Wang, Tang and Ding in 2023 by proving that the $3$-design supported by the minimum-weight codewords in their proposed cyclic dual code is isomorphic to the complementary design of the Witt spherical geometry design.
item.dc:creator: Huakai Wei, Shiyuan Qiang, Shaofang Hong

item.title: Solutions of $x^\alpha+y^\alpha=1$ in $\lambda$-Cantor sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.29793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the structure of the solutions of $x^\alpha+y^\alpha=1$ with both coordinates in a $\lambda$-Cantor set. We prove that, for any $\alpha>1$, the intersection with the middle-third Cantor set has positive Hausdorff dimension, strengthening the infinitude question posed by Jiang et al. [J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), e70408]. To explore the structure of the solutions, for arbitrary $\alpha$, we find that their Hausdorff dimension undergoes phase transitions as $\lambda$ varies: we establish the occurrence of Hausdorff phase transitions by proving the existence of zero-dimensional and positive-dimensional regions.
item.dc:creator: Kan Jiang, Nero Ziyu Li, Lifeng Xi

item.title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.29835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.
item.dc:creator: Adler Marques

item.title: Painlev\'e representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29947v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $\sigma$-Painlev\'e III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $\sigma$-Painlev\'e V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Theodoros Assiotis, Thomas Bothner, Jonathan P. Keating, Nicholas Simm, Fei Wei

item.title: On the modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
item.description: arXiv:2301.10509v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish the modularity of every elliptic curve $E/F$, where $F$ runs over infinitely many imaginary quadratic fields, including $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$ for $d=1,2,3,5$. More precisely, let $F$ be imaginary quadratic and assume that the modular curve $X_0(15)$, which is an elliptic curve of rank $0$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, also has rank $0$ over $F$. Then we prove that all elliptic curves over $F$ are modular. More generally, when $F/\mathbb{Q}$ is an imaginary CM field that does not contain a primitive fifth root of unity, we prove the modularity of elliptic curves $E/F$ under a technical assumption on the image of the representation of $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{F}/F)$ on $E[3]$ or $E[5]$. The key new technical ingredient we use is a local-global compatibility theorem for the $p$-adic Galois representations associated to torsion in the cohomology of the relevant locally symmetric spaces. We establish this result in the crystalline case, under some technical assumptions, but allowing arbitrary dimension, arbitrarily large regular Hodge--Tate weights, and allowing $p$ to be small and highly ramified in the imaginary CM field $F$.
item.dc:creator: Ana Caraiani, James Newton

item.title: Spectral mod p Satake isomorphism for GL_n
item.description: arXiv:2402.14011v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension with residue field $k$. By a work of Emerton--Gee, irreducible components inside the reduced special fiber of the moduli stack of rank $n$ \'etale $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules are labeled by Serre weights of $\mathrm{GL}_n(k)$. Let $\sigma$ be a non-Steinberg Serre weight and $\mathcal{C}_\sigma$ be the corresponding irreducible component. Motivated by the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands program, we construct a natural injective map $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{C}_\sigma) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{H}(\sigma)$ from the ring of global functions on $\mathcal{C}_\sigma$ to the Hecke algebra of $\sigma$ compatible with the mod $p$ Satake isomorphism by Herzig and Henniart--Vign\'eras in a suitable sense. For sufficiently generic $\sigma$, we prove that it is an isomorphism. As an application, we obtain a natural stratification of the irreducible component whose strata are equipped with a parabolic structure. Our main input is a construction of a morphism from an integral Hecke algebra of a generic tame type to the ring of global functions on a tamely potentially crystalline Emerton--Gee stack.
item.dc:creator: Heejong Lee

item.title: Serre weight conjectures for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$
item.description: arXiv:2510.04805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the weight part of Serre's conjecture for Galois representations valued in $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ that are tamely ramified with explicit genericity at places above $p$ as conjectured by Herzig--Tilouine and Gee--Herzig--Savitt. This improves on arXiv:2304.13879 where an inexplicit genericity hypothesis was required. As an application, we prove a modularity lifting theorem for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ under similar assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Le, Bao V. Le Hung, Heejong Lee

item.title: Numerical computations concerning Landau-Siegel zeros
item.description: arXiv:2602.03626v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We computationally verify that if $L(s,\chi)$ is a quadratic Dirichlet $L$-function modulo $q \leq 10^{10}$ then $L(\sigma,\chi) \neq 0$ for real $\sigma \ge 1-1/(5\log q)$. The number of verified moduli exceeds benchmarks due to Watkins (2004), Platt (2016), and Languasco (2023) by a factor between 66 and 25,000. Our new algorithm draws from zero-free region arguments.
item.dc:creator: Rick F. Lu, Asif Zaman, Haonan Zhao

item.title: Multivariate and quantitative Erd\H{o}s-Kac laws for Beatty sequences
item.description: arXiv:2602.04875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Erd\H{o}s-Kac theorem states that for $n$ chosen uniformly at random from $1, \dots, N$, the random variable $(\omega(n) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to the standard Gaussian as $N$ tends to infinity. Banks and Shparlinski showed that this Gaussian convergence holds for any Beatty sequence $\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor$ in place of $n$. Continuing in this spirit, Crn\v{c}evi\'c, Hern\'andez, Rizk, Sereesuchart and Tao considered the joint distribution of $\omega(n)$ and $\omega(\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor)$, which they showed to be asymptotically independent for irrational values of $\alpha$. Generalising both results, we show that for any positive integer $k$, real numbers $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k > 0$ and $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_k$, where $\alpha_i/\alpha_j$ is irrational for $i\neq j$, the joint distribution of $(\omega(\lfloor\alpha_in + \beta_i\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges to the $k$-dimensional standard Gaussian. We next discuss quantitative bounds on the rate of convergence which do not depend on the values taken by the relevant parameters. Banks and Shparlinski remarked that such quantitative bounds may be given for a single Beatty sequence $\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor$ under Diophantine type assumptions on $\alpha$. We show that such assumptions are in fact unnecessary. Specifically, for any real numbers $\alpha > 0, \beta$, we show that the Kolmogorov distance between the random variable $(\omega(\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ and the standard Gaussian is bounded above by $O(\log\log\log N/\sqrt{\log\log N})$ as $N$ tends to infinity. On the other hand, we show that universal quantitative bounds of this kind do not exist for higher-degree generalised polynomials or for the joint convergence for multiple Beatty sequences.
item.dc:creator: Fredy Yip

item.title: Exactness property of Breuil-Kisin functors and Bloch-Kato Selmer groups
item.description: arXiv:2603.26035v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a $p$-adic field and $T$ a lattice in a semistable representation of $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ with Hodge-Tate weights in $[0, r]$. Assuming $0\leq r<p-1$, we prove that for a semistable extension of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ by $T$, the corresponding sequence of strongly divisible modules is exact. Analogous statements are proved for Breuil-Kisin modules and for prismatic $F$-crystals for all $r\geq 0$. In the crystalline case, we deduce that the integral Bloch-Kato Selmer group $H^1_f(K, T)$ is computed by $\mathrm{Ext}^1$ in the category of crystalline strongly divisible modules. Using further exactness results, we define a tensor product of strongly divisible modules, which commutes with the functors to Galois representations. As an application, we show that for abelian varieties $A_1, A_2$ over $K$ with good reduction, the cup product map $\delta_1\cup\delta_2:A_1(K)\otimes A_2(K)\rightarrow H^2(K, T_p(A_1)\otimes T_p(A_2))$ induced by the Kummer sequences of $A_1, A_2$ factors through an $\mathrm{Ext}^2$ group of strongly divisible modules. In the appendix we generalize further the main exactness results to coherent reflexive $F$-gauges.
item.dc:creator: Pavel \v{C}oupek, Evangelia Gazaki, Adriano Marmora

item.title: The distribution of semi-integral points on a class of singular cubic hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.22371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $X_k$ be the cubic hypersurface defined by the equation $x^3-(y_1^2+\cdots+y_{4k}^2)z=0$. In this paper, we give an asymptotic formula for the counting function of semi-integral points on $X_k$. We also prove that this asymptotic formula agrees with Manin's conjecture for $\mathcal{M}$-points [Moe26a, Conjecture 1.4] on the $a$-invariant and the $b$-invariant.
item.dc:creator: Haruki Ito

item.title: On the sum of least prime factors in short intervals
item.description: arXiv:2608.24930v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p(n)$ denote the least prime factor of $n$ and $L_C(x)=Cx^{1/2}(\log x)^2$ with $C>0$. The sum of $p(n)/n$ over composite $n$ lying in the short interval $[x,\,x+L_C(x)]$, a question raised by Erd\H{o}s and Graham, is studied. (i) The constant $c=8$ in the mean asymptotic is estimated \[ S(x)=\sum_{{n<x,\ n\ \text{composite}}}\frac{p(n)}{n}=\frac{c\,x^{1/2}}{(\log x)^2}\Bigl(1+O\Bigl(\frac1{\log x}\Bigr)\Bigr) +O\Bigl(\frac{x^{1/3}}{\log x}\Bigr). \] (ii) For every fixed $C>0$, the window sums $\mu_C(x):=\sum_{x\le n\le x+L_C(x)}p(n)/n$ over composites have mean $4C$: $\frac1X\sum_{x\le X}\mu_C(x)=4C+O_C(1/\log X)$, and second moment $\frac1X\sum_{x\le X}(\mu_C(x)-4C)^2=O_C(1)$. (iii)Under the Maier-consistent bounded-fluctuation hypothesis, $\mu_C(x)=4C+O_C(1)$ holds uniformly in $x$, and the Erd\H{o}s--Graham question has an affirmative answer. Unconditionally, the uniform statement remains open; proving it would require resolving short-interval prime estimates at scale $(\log y)^2$.
item.dc:creator: Xu Zhang

item.title: An Explicit Belyi Map for the Wiman Sextic and Cusp Forms for a Noncongruence Subgroup
item.description: arXiv:2608.30798v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we explicitly determine an algebraic Belyi function on a unique smooth projective model $\widetilde{W}$ of the Wiman sextic curve $W$ and describe its complex uniformization in terms of modular functions associated with a certain noncongruence subgroup $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}} \subset {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. As an application, we give a direct proof of the unbounded denominators conjecture for weight $2$ cusp forms with respect to $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}}$. The conjecture is now known in full generality by the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang, following earlier progress including work of Dong, Lin, and Ng. Our proof, however, uses a degeneration of $\widetilde{W}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{5}$ together with explicit Puiseux series expansions and is substantially different from the methods employed in their work.
item.dc:creator: Madoka Horie, Takuya Yamauchi

item.title: Relative $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules and $p$-adic differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.08179v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be an affinoid rigid analytic space over a $p$-adic field, equipped with a suitable \'etale map to a unit polydisk. We provide a formalism of \emph{imperfect relative period rings} over $X$, which lie inside the corresponding perfect relative period rings constructed by Kedlaya--Liu. Then we establish a relative version of the Fontaine--Cherbonnier--Colmez equivalence between $p$-adic local systems on $X$ and \'etale $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules over such imperfect relative period rings, generalizing previous works of Andreatta--Brinon and others. Using this equivalence, we construct $p$-adic differential equations attached to de Rham local systems, carrying both geometric and arithmetic differential operators. This generalizes the work of Berger to the relative geometric setting. Along the way, we study a relative Fontaine--Sen theory on the decompletion of $\Gamma$-modules over the relative $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-period rings.
item.dc:creator: Hansheng Diao, Yong Suk Moon, Zijian Yao

item.title: A Local Proof of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for Local Epsilon Factors over Nonarchimedean Local Fields
item.description: arXiv:2609.13960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a local proof of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for local epsilon factors over nonarchimedean local fields. The lemma compares the induction expressions attached to compatible characters of distinct intermediate fields of prime degree in a bicyclic extension of prime-square degree. It is one of the main identities used in Langlands's construction of epsilon factors of local Weil representations. The proof builds on the work of Dwork, Lakkis, and Langlands. The main new point in the present paper is the wild dyadic case, i.e. biquadratic extensions over a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic two. This completes the proof of the Second Main Lemma, including the equal-characteristic case. Finally, together with the local proof of the First Main Lemma and Langlands's remaining reductions, we obtain a purely local construction of local epsilon factors envisioned by Langlands.
item.dc:creator: Fukuhiro Ueda

item.title: A Unified Framework for $p$-adic Congruences and $p$-adic Interpolations of Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.11648v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we treat the problem of determining when a sequence $\{c_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ with the exponential generating function $F(t)$ satisfies the congruence $c_{n+\ell p^k}\equiv c_n \pmod{p^{k+r}}$ for large $n$ and when its canonical interpolating functions are locally analytic. This type of congruence is often observed for several number-theoretic or combinatorial sequences, such as Bernoulli numbers, Euler numbers, and Fibonacci numbers. Traditionally, such congruences are proved by using $p$-adic integrations. In this paper, we present another approach to this problem. Instead of using $p$-adic integrals, we investigate an algebraic structure of the set of generating functions and establish some conditions on $F(t)$ that are equivalent to or sufficient for the congruence and smoothness of the interpolating functions. We also provide concrete applications of our framework to Genocchi numbers, generalized Euler numbers, and so on, which are outside the scope of the typical $p$-adic integration method.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Nishibuchi

item.title: Lie weights for CM curves and unipotent Selmer dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.12013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an equidistribution result for Galois characters in the graded Lie components $L_n$ associated to the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve $X$ over a number field $k$ with geometrically CM Jacobian. That is, we consider the $p$-adic completion of a fixed character lattice, where we define measures $\mu_n$ counting normalized character multiplicities in $L_n$, and show that $(\mu_n)_n$ weakly converges to the Haar measure. The key idea to prove convergence is to write the Fourier coefficients of $\mu_n$ in terms of traces of operators on $L_n$ induced by symplectic operators on the Tate module, and control them with a known symplectic character formula, followed by Weyl's criterion for compact abelian groups. Our main arithmetic application is to combine equidistribution with the Iwasawa-theoretic method of Coates--Kim and a compactness argument for moving analytic loci, giving a dimension inequality for unipotent Selmer schemes: $\dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}H^1_f(G_{k,T},U_n)< \dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}\prod_{v\mid p}H^1_f(G_v,U_n)$ for all sufficiently large $n,$ with the quotient having limit superior at most $1/2.$ This answers a particular case of a conjecture by Kim, from which the finiteness of $X(\mathbf{Q})$ can be recovered when $k=\mathbf{Q}.$
item.dc:creator: Ander Martin

item.title: Unconditional Bounds for Two, Three and Four Consecutive Moderate Gaps between Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
item.description: arXiv:2610.22927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove unconditional positive-proportion results for consecutive moderate gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function. More precisely, for every fixed \(0<c\leq 1/4\), the lower asymptotic densities, normalized by \(N(T)\), of the occurrences of two, three, and four consecutive gaps, each of length at least \(2\pi c/\log T\), are at least \(0.3450014\ldots\), \(0.1812517\ldots\), and \(0.0175021\ldots\), respectively. Here, zeros are ordered by ordinate and counted with multiplicity, and \(N(T)\) denotes the number of nontrivial zeros with ordinates in \((0,T]\). These bounds address the corresponding cases of a question of Gonek and Sahay. The proof combines the methods of Alp\"oge--Furman and Lamzouri with local spectral estimates and cluster counting.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Ang\'on, Erick Ross, Ze Sen Tang, Boyang Zhao

item.title: Galois Groups of Shifted Exponential Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.26873v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider the shifted truncations of the exponential series and their Galois groups: $$F_{n,a}(x) := \sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{x^j}{(a+j)!}\qquad G_{n,a}:= \text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q}).$$ In this paper we prove that for every fixed integer $a>0$, the set of $n$ for which $G_{n,a}=S_n$ has natural density one, thus answering a question of Katz and Rivin.
item.dc:creator: Shachar Weinbaum

item.title: Reduction of Decaying Navier--Stokes Turbulence to the Quantum Pendulum
item.description:
arXiv:2607.05745v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The statistics of a classical flow is a problem of quantum mechanics in loop space, and not by analogy: the loop functional of any flow is the loop-ordered exponential of the covariant derivative $\partial+\mathrm{i}v/
u$. We follow this representation from the Navier--Stokes equation to the Euler ensemble, the fixed point of the loop equation regularized by polygons with $N$ sides. Near the turning angle $ eta=\pi$ an exact operator identity, followed by an asymptotic continuum step and without a saddle-point approximation, reduces the ensemble to two quantum pendulums, the Mathieu equation; this supersedes our earlier WKB evaluation. A Monte Carlo simulation up to $N=10^5$ confirms the reduction. Extreme turbulence has singularities at small scales, and, as in quantum field theory, we define it by this regularization and a renormalization: the leading power of $N$ is removed, and the turbulent viscosity $	ilde
u$ remains as the single physical scale. This is a proposed definition of turbulence at infinite Reynolds number; its continuum spectrum is computed under a stated convergence condition, and its identification with physical turbulence is a hypothesis. The energy spectrum is a function of $\kappa=k\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$ that falls as $1/k$ and then as $k^{-2}$. At $\kappa=\sqrt2$ it has a weak nonanalyticity: its second derivative diverges logarithmically. At a fixed wave number the decay is therefore singular at the finite time $t_*=2/(	ilde
u k^2)-t_0$, when $t_*>0$, and the vorticity correlations oscillate in space with the period $\sqrt2\,\pi\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$. Of the limits of the ensemble with structure, only the pendulum limit is taken at a critical point and has a bulk dissipation that vanishes with the viscosity. A companion paper compares it with simulations and experiments.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Migdal

item.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
item.description: arXiv:2607.23453v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson, Grigore Ro\c{s}u

item.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: Local Extrema and Infinite Derivatives of the Delange Function of Base 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.21265v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Delange function of base $3$ is the continuous function $T(x)=\sum_{j\ge0}3^{-j}\tau(3^jx)$ of Takagi type, where $\tau(x)=2\min\{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathbb{Z}),1/3\}$. Multiplied by $3^n$, its values at the points $m/3^n$ are the smallest numbers $\xi_n(m)=2(nm-S_3(m))$ of edges leaving a set of $m$ vertices in the ternary Hamming cube $Q_n^3$, where $S_3(m)=\sum_{j<m}s_3(j)$ and $s_3$ is the ternary digit sum. Both facts are known. We show that the local minima of $T$ are exactly the ternary rationals $m/3^n$, and that the local maxima are exactly the points $(m+1/2)/3^n+k$ with integers $k$, $m$, $n$ such that $n\ge0$, $0\le m<3^n$ and $s_3(m)=n$. We also characterize, in terms of the ternary digits $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$ of $x$, when $T$ has an infinite derivative at $x$ from one or both sides. At a ternary rational the right derivative is $+\infty$ and the left derivative is $-\infty$. At every other point, the right derivative is $+\infty$ exactly when $\sum_{j\le n}(1-\xi_j)\to+\infty$. The condition for the left derivative to be $+\infty$ is stronger and also involves the lengths of the maximal strings of zeros among the digits. For the value $-\infty$ the two sides are exchanged and the roles of zeros and twos are swapped. In particular, $T$ has an infinite derivative at every rational point that is not a ternary rational and whose period has different numbers of zeros and twos. We also determine the maximum of $\xi_n(m)$ over every block of sizes $a3^k\le m\le(a+1)3^k$, describe by the ternary digits of $h$ the sizes $h$ for which the $h$-extra edge connectivity of $Q_n^3$ equals $\xi_n(h)$, and compute the Fourier coefficients of $T$ and its variation at each level. Finally, we determine the level set at height $3/4$, which has dimension $\log2/\log9$, and show that no level set has a larger upper box dimension and that $\{x\in[0,1]:T(x)=y\}$ is finite for almost every $y$.
item.dc:creator: Chengyi Zhu
